highlights.content: content type Featured highlight Local and Distributed Large LLM Inference with MLX and RDMA on Mac Studio ![The MLX logo](https://mlr.cdn-apple.com/media/Hero_Banner_c2c57d2d3f.png) October 15, 2026 [MLX](https://mlx-framework.org/) on Mac with Apple silicon lets AI researchers and developers experiment locally with the latest models and methods in a private environment. The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. [In a previous post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5), we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators. In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see [Figure 1](#figure1)), well above average human reading speed. Beginning on a single Mac Studio (up to 512GB of unified memory), then scaling out across multiple Macs with the RDMA over Thunderbolt driver, below we share an overview of the range of models you can now run on Mac Studio. ### Muse Spark Open Decode Speed #### Context size of 8,192 tokens Figure 1: Muse Spark Open decode speed in tokens per second, on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, at a context size of 8,192 tokens. Higher is better. We report performance for three parallelization schemes: pipeline parallelization over two Mac Studio computers (2 M5 Pipeline), and tensor parallelization over two (2 M5 Tensor) and four Mac Studio (4 M5 Tensor) computers. ## [Running Large Language Models with MLX](#running-large-language-models-with-mlx) We benchmark several popular open-weight LLMs on [Mac Studio](https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/), using the MLX LM package, as described in our [prior post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5#running--llms-on-apple-silicon). We compare two generations of Mac Studio: the recently released M5 Ultra and the previous generation, M3 Ultra. The M5 generation features the GPU Neural Accelerator, which supports dedicated matrix multiplication operations, essential for many machine learning workloads. We evaluate three frontier-class models ([Table 1](#table1)) spanning a wide range of sizes (in billions of parameters, B): the newly released Muse Spark Open (816 B), Mistral Medium 3.5 (128 B), and Qwen 3.8 (27 B). Muse Spark Open is a mixture of experts (MoE) model, which keeps only a fraction of its experts — and thus parameters — active, reducing compute at inference, and it is evaluated in NVFP4 precision. Mistral Medium 3.5 and Qwen 3.8 are dense architectures, where all parameters are active at inference, and they are evaluated in their native floating-point precision (FP8 and BF16, respectively). | Model | Total Parameters | Active Parameters | Native Precision | Evaluation Precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Muse Spark Open | 816B | 42B | BF16 | NVFP4 | | Mistral Medium 3.5 | 128B | 128B | FP8 | FP8 | | Qwen 3.8 | 27B | 27B | BF16 | BF16 | Table 1: Language models used in this post. Models ship in various precision formats; we evaluate Qwen 3.8 and Mistral Medium 3.5 in their native precision, and Muse Spark Open in 4-bit (NVFP4) precision. Our evaluation measures three metrics across a range of context sizes: time to first token (TTFT, in seconds), generation throughput (in tokens/second), and peak power usage (in watts). All the performance numbers in this post were obtained with `mlx_lm.benchmark`. For example, running Qwen 3.8 with 8,192 tokens of context and generating 128 tokens is performed with the command line: ``` mlx_lm.benchmark --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B -p 8192 -g 128 -b 1 ``` A popular use of local LLMs on Mac Studio is running agentic experiences in a private environment, including agentic coding applications that often need l...

highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Apertus 1.5 Debuts: 262K Context, Fully Open AI [2026] * [![Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/)[Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/ "Posts by Nadia Dubois") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/) October 15, 2026 12 min read Switzerland just put a number on how far “open” can go in large language models. Apertus 1.5, the second release from the Swiss AI Initiative, ships with 262,144 tokens of context, native image and audio understanding, and a training pipeline that is published down to the intermediate checkpoint. Built by EPFL, ETH Zurich, and the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), the model lands at a moment when governments and enterprises outside the United States and China are asking a blunt question: can we run frontier-adjacent AI without handing our data to a foreign cloud? Apertus 1.5 is Switzerland’s answer, and the technical paper behind it, posted to arXiv in October 2026, gives the clearest picture yet of what that answer actually contains. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Is Apertus 1.5? Apertus 1.5 is a family of two open-weight language models, sized at 8 billion and 70 billion parameters, released by the Swiss AI Initiative as a continued-pretraining successor to the original Apertus 1.0. According to the release notes published on Hugging Face, the project describes itself as one of the world’s largest fully open language model efforts, built entirely by [ETH Zurich, EPFL, and CSCS](https://huggingface.co/blog/swiss-ai/apertus-v15-release-notes). Unlike most “open” model releases that hand over only the final weights, Apertus publishes training data sourcing, data-preparation methods, training recipes, evaluation suites, alignment principles, and intermediate checkpoints spanning base, supervised fine-tuning, RLVR, DPO, and SDPO stages. That level of disclosure is the point. Apertus is less a product launch than a sovereignty statement: a working demonstration that a mid-sized European country, without the capital of a Microsoft, Google, or Alibaba, can train, document, and ship a model competitive with other open-weight systems. The timing matters too. Apertus 1.5 arrives in the same window as Meta’s [Muse Spark Open](https://tech-insider.org/meta-muse-spark-open-mac-studio-2026/) and Nvidia’s [Nemotron 3.5 Super VL](https://tech-insider.org/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-2026/), both released on October 15, 2026, turning this week into one of the busiest stretches for open-weight model drops this year. ## Inside the Numbers: Parameters, Context Window and Training Data The jump from Apertus 1.0 to 1.5 is substantial on paper. The 8B model received 4 trillion additional training tokens, bringing its total to roughly 19 trillion tokens, while the 70B model received 2 trillion additional tokens for a total near 17 trillion. The context window grew to 262,144 tokens, a fourfold increase over the original Apertus, according to the [AI Weekly release summary](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/swiss-ai-opens-apertus-15-with-262k-context-multimodal-weights-and-4t-added-pre). highlights.content: # Revenium Is Enlisting The Channel To Bring Its AI Cost Control Tech To Enterprises: Exclusive With the new Revenium partner program, the company is looking to recruit a broad range of partners including systems integrators, MSPs, resellers and distributors, and OEM/ISV technology partners. Revenium today launched its inaugural partner program to recruit and support systems integrators, MSPs, resellers and other partners to work with the company’s new AI cost control software. Through the new program, startup Revenium is looking to work with channel partners to help businesses and organizations address questions about how—and how much—they are spending on agentic AI systems and how much of a return they are getting on their AI investments. The program launch comes as more businesses and organizations are scaling up their AI development projects from early-stage pilots to full production. As they do so, they often discover they have no real way to measure whether their efforts are paying off and generating the anticipated ROI. [Related: Bigger AI Security Budgets Should Be Coming In 2027: GuidePoint CISO] “We see this as an enablement journey for AI adoption,” said Matt Small, Revenium vice president of customer success and partner program lead, discussing the company’s technology in an exclusive interview with CRN. “It’s a tool to define the value and worth of AI-assisted and AI-authored work in the enterprise.” Revenium, founded in 2021, originally focused on developing API metering and monetization technology that evolved into the AI cost control offering the company debuted in March of this year. In November 2025, Revenium, headquartered in Herndon, Va., raised $13.5 million in a seed funding round led by Two Bear Capital with participation from WestWave Capital. Small (pictured) said the AI control system concept comes from the world of industrial controls where systems track real-time activity and real-time data and take action if things go wrong. “The important aspect for us is that the control system works end to end,” he said. “It’s not just, ‘Hey, I sent you an alert that something happened, and an agent ran off and spent $10,000 last night.’” Small said the Revenium system can detect when an agent is “about to go off the rails” and stop it, provide a post-mortem of what happened, and offer insights to prevent similar problems in the future. “If you’re delegating work to autonomous agents, then you need real-time budgets and guardrails in place to direct their flow,” Small said. The increased need for visibility and control around how AI agents are behaving has given rise to a wave of agentic observability and governance products in the market, such as those from Galileo Technologies (acquired by Cisco in April) and Arize (acquired by Dynatrace in August). Small notes that Revenium doesn’t define its product as an observability tool. “We always say observability answers what happened, but it doesn’t answer whether or not it was worth it,” he said. “Revenium calculates the worth and the value of the outputs…the ROI of the actual AI-orchestrated workflows or assisted processes.” ## The Revenium Partner Program Why launch a partner program now? Small said when businesses deploy AI systems and run into performance and cost problems, “There’s a wake-up moment in there—especially for very large enterprises—and the first people they call, typically, is their trusted delivery partner.” “So the AI transformation moment is ripe for partners, especially systems integrators, services providers, even technology vendors, that can get in there and help companies organize this chaos,” he said. With the Revenium partner program, which is now up and running, the company is recruiting systems integrators, managed service providers, resellers, technology distributors and ISVs that can leverage the Revenium AI cost control offering into a service they deliver, a product they can resell, or capabilities they can build into their own platf...

highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Agentic Martech Surge: 8 Tools Ship in 14 Days [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 15, 2026 · 13 min read Eight AI-powered marketing platforms launched, rebranded, or changed hands in a single two-week stretch this month, and the pattern behind them says more about where marketing technology is headed than any single product. Between October 1 and October 12, 2026, vendors ranging from a ten-year-old content platform to a two-person loyalty-tech startup all shipped the same basic idea: hand marketing work to an AI agent instead of a dashboard. The trade press, led by MarTech.org, has been tracking the wave in near-real time, and the throughline is unmistakable. AI martech has stopped being about generating copy faster. It’s about letting software run campaigns, measure brand visibility inside chatbots, and reallocate budget on its own. This matters beyond the marketing department. Every one of these launches plugs an AI agent into a company’s customer data, ad accounts, or content library, often through the same Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors that engineering teams use to wire Claude or ChatGPT into internal systems. That overlap, half marketing stack and half AI infrastructure, is why this cluster of announcements reads as much like a software story as an advertising one. ## A Two-Week Sprint Reshapes AI Martech The timeline is tight. Contentstack and Kargo both went generally available with new AI products on October 1, 2026. Zeta Global unveiled its AthenaOS platform on October 8. Hightouch announced it had acquired Strata on October 9. In between, smaller vendors including Aiseogic, Antavo, Apollo, ClicData, CommerceIQ, ContentPen, PostcardMania, Tealium, Toluna, and 10Fold all rolled out AI features of their own, according to [MarTech’s ongoing coverage of AI-powered martech releases](https://martech.org/topic/marketing-artificial-intelligence-ai/). None of these companies coordinated the timing, but the shared logic is hard to miss. Buyers increasingly ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or Claude for product recommendations instead of searching Google, and marketers have no reliable way to see what those models are telling prospective customers. That gap is driving a new product category, loosely called answer-engine optimization (AEO), alongside a parallel push into agentic execution: platforms that don’t just recommend a budget shift but make it. ## Contentstack’s Canoe Puts a Price Tag on AI Visibility Contentstack launched Contentstack Canoe on October 1, 2026, at ContentCon Europe in Amsterdam. Canoe scans a company’s website, maps its products and buyer personas, and tracks up to ten competitors, then generates the questions real buyers are likely to ask an AI assistant and sorts them by stage of the buying journey, according to coverage from [The Agile Brand Guide](https://agilebrandguide.com/yesterdays-marketing-technology-ai-news-october-10-2026/). Pricing follows a freemium model: a Free plan at $0 checks how a brand shows up in ChatGPT and Gemini once a month, while a Growth plan at $279 a month (or $2,790 billed annually) adds Perplexity and Claude to the monitoring mix. Contentstack has pencilled in an Enterprise tier for early 2027. The product sits squarely in the AEO category that Contentstack, Tealium, and ContentPen are all now racing to own, each wagering that marketers will pay recurring fees just to find out what an AI chatbot says about them. ## Kargo’s Karlo Brings Agentic Media Buying Downmarket Kargo made Karlo generally available the same day as Canoe, positioning it as a self-serve, agentic media-buying tool aimed at small businesses that have never had an in-house media-buying team or an agency retainer. AI Agents.content: # Revenium Is Enlisting The Channel To Bring Its AI Cost Control Tech To Enterprises: Exclusive With the new Revenium partner program, the company is looking to recruit a broad range of partners including systems integrators, MSPs, resellers and distributors, and OEM/ISV technology partners. Revenium today launched its inaugural partner program to recruit and support systems integrators, MSPs, resellers and other partners to work with the company’s new AI cost control software. Through the new program, startup Revenium is looking to work with channel partners to help businesses and organizations address questions about how—and how much—they are spending on agentic AI systems and how much of a return they are getting on their AI investments. The program launch comes as more businesses and organizations are scaling up their AI development projects from early-stage pilots to full production. As they do so, they often discover they have no real way to measure whether their efforts are paying off and generating the anticipated ROI. [Related: Bigger AI Security Budgets Should Be Coming In 2027: GuidePoint CISO] “We see this as an enablement journey for AI adoption,” said Matt Small, Revenium vice president of customer success and partner program lead, discussing the company’s technology in an exclusive interview with CRN. “It’s a tool to define the value and worth of AI-assisted and AI-authored work in the enterprise.” Revenium, founded in 2021, originally focused on developing API metering and monetization technology that evolved into the AI cost control offering the company debuted in March of this year. In November 2025, Revenium, headquartered in Herndon, Va., raised $13.5 million in a seed funding round led by Two Bear Capital with participation from WestWave Capital. Small (pictured) said the AI control system concept comes from the world of industrial controls where systems track real-time activity and real-time data and take action if things go wrong. “The important aspect for us is that the control system works end to end,” he said. “It’s not just, ‘Hey, I sent you an alert that something happened, and an agent ran off and spent $10,000 last night.’” Small said the Revenium system can detect when an agent is “about to go off the rails” and stop it, provide a post-mortem of what happened, and offer insights to prevent similar problems in the future. “If you’re delegating work to autonomous agents, then you need real-time budgets and guardrails in place to direct their flow,” Small said. The increased need for visibility and control around how AI agents are behaving has given rise to a wave of agentic observability and governance products in the market, such as those from Galileo Technologies (acquired by Cisco in April) and Arize (acquired by Dynatrace in August). Small notes that Revenium doesn’t define its product as an observability tool. “We always say observability answers what happened, but it doesn’t answer whether or not it was worth it,” he said. “Revenium calculates the worth and the value of the outputs…the ROI of the actual AI-orchestrated workflows or assisted processes.” ## The Revenium Partner Program Why launch a partner program now? Small said when businesses deploy AI systems and run into performance and cost problems, “There’s a wake-up moment in there—especially for very large enterprises—and the first people they call, typically, is their trusted delivery partner.” “So the AI transformation moment is ripe for partners, especially systems integrators, services providers, even technology vendors, that can get in there and help companies organize this chaos,” he said. With the Revenium partner program, which is now up and running, the company is recruiting systems integrators, managed service providers, resellers, technology distributors and ISVs that can leverage the Revenium AI cost control offering into a service they deliver, a product they can resell, or capabilities they can build into their own platf...

AI Agents.content: [![Ledger Academy](https://www.ledger.com/wp-content/themes/ledger-v2/public/images/ledger-academy-logo-long.svg)](https://www.ledger.com/academy "Ledger Academy") Upgrade your digital life Ledger Wallet: Free from compromise [Download now](https://shop.ledger.com/pages/ledger-wallet#download-ledger-wallet "Download now") [Learn more](https://www.ledger.com/blog-release-notes-q2-2026-free-from-compromise "Learn more") # Introducing Ledger Agent Intent By **Ledger** Oct 15, 2026 | **Updated Oct 15, 2026** Read 8 min | | | --- | | KEY TAKEAWAYS: | | — Ledger Agent Intent is the next third-party tool addition to Ledger’s security stack for artificial intelligence (AI) agents.  — Ledger Agent Intent lets agents propose actions within policies you set, while you approve each one on your Ledger signer, where your private keys are designed to stay. — An agent such as OpenClaw can check balances, prepare swaps, or rebalance staking positions, while actions that move funds are designed to wait for your approval on your Ledger signer. | Agentic AI is moving from answering questions to completing tasks. Tools like OpenClaw, an open-source agent that acts as a digital employee on your own computer, and Meta’s Muse, which can send emails and book travel, show how quickly that shift is happening. For crypto users, the potential is significant too. In an [agentic wallet](https://www.ledger.com/academy/glossary/agentic-wallet), an [AI agent](https://www.ledger.com/academy/glossary/ai-agents) watches markets around the clock and prepares transactions, payments, and routine portfolio tasks within parameters you set. AI is already acting on your behalf. The question is whether you control what it does. Ledger Agent Intent is built to give you that control, and it is one layer of the Ledger Agent Stack described in [Ledger’s 2026 AI Security Roadmap](https://www.ledger.com/blog-2026-ai-security-roadmap). To be useful, an agent needs access to the things it acts on, such as email, files, credentials, and wallets, and that same access makes mistakes and manipulation costly. The Agent Stack answers with one principle. Agents propose. You approve. Your Ledger signer enforces. ## What is Ledger Agent Intent? Think of each suggestion from Ledger Agent Intent as a proposal, not a transaction. When operating within the policy that you set, your agent can propose transactions that align with your overall goals, such as spending limits or specific transaction types. Each proposal is designed to require physical confirmation on your Ledger signer, the device that keeps your private keys offline, before the transaction is broadcast to the blockchain. You still have to review the proposal, and the transaction is designed not to move forward until you do. The proposal appears in the Ledger Agent Intent interface. Confirming it happens on your Ledger signer itself, the same action required for any transaction. Ledger Agent Intent gives every request for your approval one place to land. Your agents keep working on everything else, and each proposal waits in your queue until you are ready to review it. If you run several agents, their requests arrive in the same queue. Your AI agent can watch for the conditions you care about and prepare the matching action, whether that is a swap when a price you chose is reached, a staking position that needs rebalancing, or funds that are ready to collect. It can be as aggressive or reserved as you prompt it. It isn’t realistic to sit in front of a computer all hours of the day, waiting for an opportunity to align with your goals, so you don’t have to. Your agent waits until an opportunity or task comes up, and then proposes the transaction on your behalf. All you have to do is decide if you want to confirm it. That really is the point behind an intent: getting the benefit of an AI agent that knows your goals and handles the legwork for you, while you remain the final approval. ## How Ledger Agent Intent Bridges AI & Self-Cust...

AI Agents.content: ![Microsoft](https://uhf.microsoft.com/images/microsoft/RE1Mu3b.png) Discover what’s coming to Microsoft Ignite, Nov 17-20, 2026. [Register now.](https://ignite.microsoft.com/home?wt.mc_ID=msignite26_ciarmar_corp_np_oo_CopilotStudio_BlogBnrCoPltStdo_0434) ![](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/blog/copilot-studio/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/agents-delegate-processes-3.jpg) # Delegate shared business processes to agents that are more persistent and proactive with Microsoft Copilot Studio ## Listen to this post ## Share ## Content types ## Topics The nature of work is changing rapidly on two levels with the advancements in technology: how each individual gets work done, and how work gets done across the organization. This creates two complementary opportunities for the latest in agentic capabilities—greater individual productivity and organizational process transformation. In September 2026, Microsoft announced the [next evolution of Copilot](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/09/25/introducing-the-new-copilot-with-home-code-and-autopilot/), designed to be more personalized and proactive for each person. Process transformation can benefit from something complementary: managed agents that belong to the organization, persist beyond any one individual’s role or tenure, work where the process happens, start work when needed, carry context forward, and improve over time. Today, we’re announcing features in [Copilot Studio](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/products/copilot-studio) that empower you to build those managed agents for your business processes. Agent accounts and business process memory allow users to delegate real work to digital teammates in the apps and services they already use. Together with triggers in the GitHub Copilot harness, these features extend Copilot Studio as the platform for building persistent, proactive agents in the flow of work. ## Rethink how people, systems, and administrators work with agents [**Agent accounts**](https://aka.ms/persistentagents/accounts) allow agents to work in Microsoft 365 with their own credentials, similar to how any person would. People can now invoke the agent in [Microsoft Teams](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-teams/group-chat-software) and Outlook to ask questions, assign work, or contribute updates without a separate agent chat for every task. ![Animation showing a user giving an agent its own account in Microsoft Copilot Studio.](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/blog/copilot-studio/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Give-an-agent-an-account.gif) These agents can be @mentioned, like any process participant, in comments of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, to jump into work. Team members can also delegate process tasks to the agent via Teams or email and keep working, while the agent continues the task between their interactions. ![Animation showing an agent providing a task update in Microsoft Teams.](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/blog/copilot-studio/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Agent-providing-update-in-Teams.gif) Accounts also enable agents to work with other agents, tools, apps, and services using their own approved credentials and scoped permissions, without relying on any individual user’s or maker’s credentials. This means work can be attributed to the agents, while process owners retain control over its scope. This clearer attribution increases observability and traceability, helping process owners understand which actions were taken by agents and which were taken by people. Agent accounts support additional controls for administrators too. They can now scope access, have additional controls, and manage lifecycle for these agents. Additional access policies, quality, cost management, and lifecycle controls specific to these agents are planned for in the coming months. ![Animation showing an administrator viewing and managing an agent account in the Power Platform admin center.](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/blog/copilot-studio/wp-c...

Forum is a standalone Groups app that a small team built from scratch. It’s also where we tested a different way of working: treating an AI agent as a participant in the engineering process rather than a faster way to type. That experiment needed a definition of success, and ours wasn’t code volume. We measured verified, production-ready outcomes — changes that build, pass tests, and survive review.  ## From Human-In-The-Loop to Human-On-The-Loop Pointing AI at the coding step alone doesn’t change much. Our results compounded as we extended the approach to the stages around implementation — planning, building, testing, and verification. The clearest way to see the shift is in who owns each step. With **human-in-the-loop**, the engineer drives every step and the AI assists inside it by autocompleting a function, suggesting a fix, or answering a question. Each iteration advances at the pace of the person driving it. With **human-on-the-loop**, the agent runs the iteration itself — plan, implement, build, test, correct, repeat — while the engineer sets the goal, watches the run, steps in when it drifts, and approves the result. The person’s job moves from executing the steps to owning the outcome and holding the quality bar. This is the target we are driving toward, not a finished state: some stages run autonomously today, while others still keep an engineer in each iteration. When the engineer supervises, work stops being strictly sequential. Cycles that used to run one at a time can overlap, and an engineer’s time goes to direction and judgment rather than to sitting through the loop. But that only holds if what comes back can be trusted. Without verification, AI-generated code creates a familiar problem — plausible output that no one has confirmed actually works, which an engineer then has to read, debug, and often discard. Weak signals don’t remove the constraint; they move it from writing code to reviewing code that looks finished and isn’t. So we set the bar at verification rather than compilation. Compiling isn’t the finish line — a task is complete only once automated tests and visual checks have passed. Agents check their own work before an engineer sees it, which means what reaches review is a smaller...

The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. [In a previous post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5), we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators. In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see [Figure 1](#figure1)), well above average human reading speed. Beginning on a single Mac Studio (up to 512GB of unified memory), then scaling out across multiple Macs with the RDMA over Thunderbolt driver, below we share an overview of the range of models you can now run on Mac Studio. ### Muse Spark Open Decode Speed #### Context size of 8,192 tokens Figure 1: Muse Spark Open decode speed in tokens per second, on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, at a context size of 8,192 tokens. Higher is better. We report performance for three parallelization schemes: pipeline parallelization over two Mac Studio computers (2 M5 Pipeline), and tensor parallelization over two (2 M5 Tensor) and four Mac Studio (4 M5 Tensor) computers. ## [Running Large Language Models with MLX](#running-large-language-models-with-mlx) We benchmark several popular open-weight LLMs on [Mac Studio](https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/), using the MLX LM package, as described in our [prior post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5#running--llms-on-apple-silicon). We compare two generations of Mac Studio: the recently released M5 Ultra and the previous generation, M3 Ultra. The M5 generation features the GPU Neural Accelerator, which supports dedicated matrix multiplication operations, essential for many machine learning workloads. We evaluate three frontier-class models ([Table 1](#table1)) spanning a wide range of sizes (in billions of parameters, B): the newly released Muse Spark Open (816 B), Mistral Medium 3.5 (128 B), and Qwen 3.8 (27 B). Muse Spark Open is a mixture of experts (MoE) model, which keeps only a fraction of its experts — and thus parameters — active, reducing compute at inference, and it is evaluated in NVFP4 precision. Mistral Medium 3.5 and Qwen 3.8 are dense architectures, where all parameters are active at inference, and they are evaluated in their native floating-point precision (FP8 and BF16, respectively). | Model | Total Parameters | Active Parameters | Native Precision | Evaluation Precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Muse Spark Open | 816B | 42B | BF16 | NVFP4 | | Mistral Medium 3.5 | 128B | 128B | FP8 | FP8 | | Qwen 3.8 | 27B | 27B | BF16 | BF16 | Table 1: Language models used in this post. Models ship in various precision formats; we evaluate Qwen 3.8 and Mistral Medium 3.5 in their native precision, and Muse Spark Open in 4-bit (NVFP4) precision. This upgrade brings model performance, pricing, capabilities, input and output requirements, reliability, and task-specific results into one comparison experience, helping users choose the right AI models for their project needs and budgets. **Highlights of The AI Leaderboard Tool** ### Compare Leading Models Across LLM, Video, Image , and Audio The AI Leaderboard enables users to explore and compare models across 4 major categories on one dashboard: LLMs (GPT-6 Astra, Claude, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek), video ([**Seedance 2.5**](https://crun.ai/models/seedance-2-5), Kling, Veo, Grok Imagine), image (GPT Image 2.5, Nano Banana, Seedream), and audio (Suno, Qwen3-TTS). ### Explore Benchmarks, Capabilities, Pricing, and Context Windows Selecting an AI model involves more than identifying a top-ranked option. The leaderboard enables users to evaluate relevant metrics and specifications, including performance benchmarks, supported capabilities, pricing, context windows where applicable, input and output capabilities, task success rates, and reliability. Apertus 1.5, the second release from the Swiss AI Initiative, ships with 262,144 tokens of context, native image and audio understanding, and a training pipeline that is published down to the intermediate checkpoint. Built by EPFL, ETH Zurich, and the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), the model lands at a moment when governments and enterprises outside the United States and China are asking a blunt question: can we run frontier-adjacent AI without handing our data to a foreign cloud? Apertus 1.5 is Switzerland’s answer, and the technical paper behind it, posted to arXiv in October 2026, gives the clearest picture yet of what that answer actually contains. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. Unlike most “open” model releases that hand over only the final weights, Apertus publishes training data sourcing, data-preparation methods, training recipes, evaluation suites, alignment principles, and intermediate checkpoints spanning base, supervised fine-tuning, RLVR, DPO, and SDPO stages. That level of disclosure is the point. LLMs.content: [Skip To Main Content](#primary-content) [News](/content/www/us/en/newsroom/home.html) # Intel Offers Day-0 Support for Meta's Muse Spark Open Data Center Silicon Built for 816B Scale Copied [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](/content/www/us/en/newsroom/home.html#aiartificialintelligence) ![](https://intelcorp.scene7.com/is/image/intelcorp/adobestock-2117319102?qlt=80&ts=1789739650705&dpr=off) Meta’s official open-weight release of Muse Spark Open, an 816 billion-parameter any-to-text model, represents a major milestone in multimodal AI and the most capable U.S. open-weights model released to date. Deploying an 816 billion-parameter architecture requires extreme memory efficiency and hardware-level low-precision acceleration. Intel has enabled day-0 support across Intel® Xeon® processors and Intel data center GPU platforms, Intel® GPU D-series, through targeted low-bit model quantization. Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model. Trained specifically for agentic coding workflows, it delivers higher first-attempt accuracy, reliable tool calling and deep codebase understanding across the repositories developers use. This open-weight model is strong in code generation, debugging and codebase understanding. The 1 million-token context window handles entire projects, including complex dependencies, legacy code and thousands of files, without requiring tasks to be broken into smaller pieces. Muse Spark Open also supports multimodal understanding, including audio, video, image and document comprehension. For agentic use cases, Muse Spark Open was built to plan, act, observe and self-correct over extended workflows. It is trained to browse the web, including multimodal content, use an agentic harness to spawn and coordinate subagents for decomposable work, and leverage computer-use capabilities across desktop, mobile and browser environments. **Data Center Silicon Built for 816 Billion-Parameter Scale** Large language models at the scale of Meta’s Muse Spark Open highlight the growing infrastructure demands of advanced AI workloads. At hundreds of billions of parameters, they require substantial memory capacity, efficient low-precision compute, power efficiency and architectures that can bring these capabilities into existing data center footprints. Muse Spark Open has been tested and is running on the upcoming Intel data center GPU, Intel® GPU D-series, today. This early work reflects Intel’s commitment to day-0 support for emerging AI models and gives customers an early path to begin evaluating Muse Spark Open on Intel silicon. The image above shows Muse Spark Open inference running on four Intel® GPU D-series GPUs. Each GPU provides 160 GB of memory, offering sufficient capacity to run Muse Spark Open across four GPUs. Intel® GPU D-series is designed for the demands of large and agentic AI models. Built on the Intel® Xe3P architecture, it features: * 32 Xe3P cores * 256 Intel® XMX engines * Dedicated hardware acceleration across a broad range of data types, including MXFP4 * 160 GB LPDDR5x memory capacity, with options up to 480 GB These capabilities are well aligned with large-model inference, combining low-precision compute with high memory capacity to support models such as Muse Spark Open efficiently. Its 350W air-cooled PCIe form factor also simplifies deployment. A compact four-card configuration can host an 816 billion-parameter-class model within conventional air-cooled data center racks, helping reduce infrastructure complexity for organizations evaluating frontier-scale AI. ![](https://intelcorp.scene7.com/is/image/intelcorp/newsroom-0day-code?qlt=80&ts=1789740455603&dpr=off) **Muse Spark Open on Intel® Xeon® Processors** Designed for high-capacity CPU inference, Intel® Xeon® processors support INT4 weight-only quantized (WOQ) inference, reducing memory footprint while leveraging Intel® Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel® AMX) to accelerate AI matrix operations. LLMs.content: # Microsoft Unveils 2.8 Trillion-Parameter AI Model, Claiming 4–12x Efficiency Gains Over DeepSeek ##### Key Elements ![Microsoft Unveils 2.8 Trillion-Parameter AI Model, Claiming 4–12x Efficiency Gains Over DeepSeek](https://img.biggo.com/uyy_lI6LuMA4eJGf6RjSWmI9sa5kM81TDw2NMmOmHMk/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwLzYyODU2NWViLTdjYzYtNDZiNS1hNjFmLThiZTZmY2JlYmM1Yl8xNzkyMTE4NDg1X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Microsoft announced on its official blog on the 16th that it has completed pre-training of "MAI-Base-2," a next-generation foundation model with a total of 2.8 trillion parameters. The company claims the model reduces the compute required to achieve the same performance as the latest model from Chinese AI firm DeepSeek by up to 12x. The new model is the successor to "MAI-Base-1," which was unveiled in June. Training was conducted over 38 days from August to September using 16,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs, consuming approximately 50 trillion training tokens. Visual data, including images, accounted for 18% of the total. MAI-Base-2 adopts a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture. Of the 2.8 trillion total parameters, only about 80 billion are activated during actual inference. The design activates only the necessary expert networks based on input data, allowing the model to scale up in size while reducing computational burden. Microsoft explained that it improved GPU utilization efficiency by simultaneously refining the model architecture and training algorithms. In particular, the company optimized memory management for the MoE structure, raising model compute utilization in that segment from 24% to 35%. The "Muon" optimization algorithm and gradient adjustment techniques were also applied for training stability. According to Microsoft's internal evaluation results, MAI-Base-2 outperformed all major open-weight models used as benchmarks. Compared to DeepSeek's "DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base," the model reduced the compute required to achieve equivalent performance by 4.2x to 12.3x. Training efficiency improved 6.3x to 12.7x compared to the previous MAI-Base-1. There were also changes on the training data front. Unique training data used for MAI-Base-2 increased by approximately 36% compared to the previous model. Microsoft emphasized that it used only proprietary source data rather than distillation methods that learn from other AI models' outputs. This is also a prerequisite for licensing model weights to trusted partners. The model was designed as a vision-language model (VLM) that trains on text and images together from the start. Without a separate image encoder, it can handle various visual tasks including document and chart analysis, spatial reasoning, and computer use. Microsoft is currently conducting post-training and plans to release additional performance evaluation results in the future. The company is pursuing plans to offer model weights to enterprise customers through its AI platform "Microsoft Foundry." General availability timing and pricing have not yet been disclosed. The company also announced it has begun preparations for developing the next model, "MAI-Base-3." The vision is to continuously enhance AI performance and cost competitiveness by optimizing proprietary models and infrastructure together. Meanwhile, notable results have emerged from large-scale software rewriting experiments using AI. Developer Theo Browne unveiled a project using AI agents to port core TypeScript development tools to the Rust language. His creation, "TS\_Rust," reportedly achieved speeds approximately 12.5x faster than existing TypeScript implementations and about 2x faster than Microsoft's in-development Go-based implementation. However, these figures come from the developer's own testing and require independent verification. Browne explained that he initially used OpenAI models for the project but spent over $400,000 (approximately 540 million won) at API pricing while only achieving about 84% com...

LLMs.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/10/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/10/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/10/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/10/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### October 15, 2026 ### October 14, 2026 ## AtScale Research Shows Semantic Layers Double AI Accuracy *Leading AI models get fewer than four in ten business queries right without a semantic layer, exposing a critical barrier to AI moving into financial, operational, and other business-critical workflows. Every model improved, and an open-weight model kept pace with frontier models.* BOSTON, Oct. 15, 2026 — [AtScale](https://www.atscale.com/), a leading provider of the universal semantic layer for enterprise AI and analytics, today released research showing that adding its semantic layer doubled AI accuracy on business questions on average 1.7x to 2.4x with it, with gains on all seven AI models tested. The findings demonstrate how shared business definitions and governed computation can help enterprises improve AI reliability as they expand adoption across finance, sales, and operations. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/07/atscale-neg-white-300x166.png)](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/07/atscale-neg-white.png)As businesses race to adopt the latest AI models, many overlook a more fundamental question: does the AI understand what their business data actually means? Without that understanding, even the strongest model has to guess at definitions like revenue, margin, and active customer. In AtScale’s research, leading models answered fewer than four in ten business questions correctly when they queried the database directly, even with the schema, column documentation and business glossary provided. That gap is what keeps AI out of the financial and operational workflows where the numbers have to be right. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/07/atscale-neg-white-300x166.png) AtScale conducted the research using BIRD-Interact, an independently developed benchmark with 600 tasks across 22 databases. 410 of the tasks are business questions, and 317 of those have a verifiable correct answer. Its ambiguous questions, purposefully messy data, and simulated-user conversations reflect challenges encountered in enterprise AI workflows. **The principal findings:** Jay Schuren, President, AtScale, added: “Large language models are probabilistic by design. Finance and operations demand consistent, auditable answers. That mismatch is one of the biggest barriers to putting enterprise AI into production. A semantic layer bridges the gap: the model reasons about the question, while governed business definitions and deterministic computation produce the answer. That’s how AI agents move from experimentation into the workflows that run the business, and how model providers unlock the next wave of enterprise adoption.” For customers, the value extends beyond a benchmark score: a shared definition of revenue across finance and sales, consistent calculations across agents and dashboards over time, and the freedom to adopt new AI models without rebuilding business logic. AtScale gives enterprises a governed foundation for moving AI into everyday decisions, with a repeatable way to measure and improve accuracy as their business evolves. The research supports [**AtScale for AI**](https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/this-just-in/atscale-launches-atscale-for-ai-to-close-the-enterprise-ai-accuracy-gap/), announced separately today, which brings together semantic modeling, question clarification, governed computation, and accuracy evalu...

AI Product.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Agentic Martech Surge: 8 Tools Ship in 14 Days [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 15, 2026 · 13 min read Eight AI-powered marketing platforms launched, rebranded, or changed hands in a single two-week stretch this month, and the pattern behind them says more about where marketing technology is headed than any single product. Between October 1 and October 12, 2026, vendors ranging from a ten-year-old content platform to a two-person loyalty-tech startup all shipped the same basic idea: hand marketing work to an AI agent instead of a dashboard. The trade press, led by MarTech.org, has been tracking the wave in near-real time, and the throughline is unmistakable. AI martech has stopped being about generating copy faster. It’s about letting software run campaigns, measure brand visibility inside chatbots, and reallocate budget on its own. This matters beyond the marketing department. Every one of these launches plugs an AI agent into a company’s customer data, ad accounts, or content library, often through the same Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors that engineering teams use to wire Claude or ChatGPT into internal systems. That overlap, half marketing stack and half AI infrastructure, is why this cluster of announcements reads as much like a software story as an advertising one. ## A Two-Week Sprint Reshapes AI Martech The timeline is tight. Contentstack and Kargo both went generally available with new AI products on October 1, 2026. Zeta Global unveiled its AthenaOS platform on October 8. Hightouch announced it had acquired Strata on October 9. In between, smaller vendors including Aiseogic, Antavo, Apollo, ClicData, CommerceIQ, ContentPen, PostcardMania, Tealium, Toluna, and 10Fold all rolled out AI features of their own, according to [MarTech’s ongoing coverage of AI-powered martech releases](https://martech.org/topic/marketing-artificial-intelligence-ai/). None of these companies coordinated the timing, but the shared logic is hard to miss. Buyers increasingly ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, or Claude for product recommendations instead of searching Google, and marketers have no reliable way to see what those models are telling prospective customers. That gap is driving a new product category, loosely called answer-engine optimization (AEO), alongside a parallel push into agentic execution: platforms that don’t just recommend a budget shift but make it. ## Contentstack’s Canoe Puts a Price Tag on AI Visibility Contentstack launched Contentstack Canoe on October 1, 2026, at ContentCon Europe in Amsterdam. Canoe scans a company’s website, maps its products and buyer personas, and tracks up to ten competitors, then generates the questions real buyers are likely to ask an AI assistant and sorts them by stage of the buying journey, according to coverage from [The Agile Brand Guide](https://agilebrandguide.com/yesterdays-marketing-technology-ai-news-october-10-2026/). Pricing follows a freemium model: a Free plan at $0 checks how a brand shows up in ChatGPT and Gemini once a month, while a Growth plan at $279 a month (or $2,790 billed annually) adds Perplexity and Claude to the monitoring mix. Contentstack has pencilled in an Enterprise tier for early 2027. The product sits squarely in the AEO category that Contentstack, Tealium, and ContentPen are all now racing to own, each wagering that marketers will pay recurring fees just to find out what an AI chatbot says about them. ## Kargo’s Karlo Brings Agentic Media Buying Downmarket Kargo made Karlo generally available the same day as Canoe, positioning it as a self-serve, agentic media-buying tool aimed at small businesses that have never had an in-house media-buying team or an agency retainer. AI Product.content: ![](https://www.techtarget.com/rms/onlineimages/ai_a373894778_searchsitetablet_520X173.jpg) putilov\_denis - stock.adobe.com # Should CIOs bet on Meta's new enterprise technology push? ## Meta is carving out an enterprise offering after years of consumer-first focus. How seriously should IT leaders evaluate Meta as an enterprise vendor? ![Sean Michael Kerner](https://cdn.ttgtmedia.com/rms/onlineImages/kerner_sean.jpg) Meta has entered the enterprise technology space. On Sept. 28, the company [announced](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/launching-meta-enterprise-platform/) its Meta Enterprise Platform, a new offering and business unit focused on offering AI agents and developer tools to companies. Whether CIOs should bet on [Meta's enterprise AI push](https://www.techtarget.com/ai/news/366651790/Meta-joins-enterprise-agent-race-with-Muse-Wonder-facing-a-trust-gap) is a challenge to answer. Meta, the company formerly known as Facebook, is still best known for its social media properties including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. In recent years, it has made a concerted effort to be a generative AI player as well, with somewhat mixed success. The company's [Llama models](https://www.techtarget.com/whatis/feature/Meta-Llama-4-explained-Everything-you-need-to-know) were notable for being open source and letting others build on them. Meta shifted its strategy with the Muse platform, offering proprietary technology designed to compete with industry rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic. "The problem is that for customers to adopt AI, they have to be able to trust it, and Meta's track record on trust is not great," said Rebecca Wettemann, CEO and principal analyst at Valoir. ## Meta's enterprise pivot in context The initial release announcement for the Meta Enterprise Platform described the offering as the way Meta will offer its technology stack to businesses and developers. CJ Desai, the former MongoDB CEO, will lead the unit as chief enterprise platform officer and report directly to Mark Zuckerberg. Meta Enterprise Platform started out as four key products: Meta's enterprise move puts it into [an already crowded market](https://www.techtarget.com/ai/feature/Vertical-AI-agents-explained-The-future-of-enterprise-tech) with offerings from Microsoft, Amazon, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Salesforce, among others. "Meta owns the chat window where the customer actually shows up. So, the honest shortlist question is not whether Meta replaces Copilot or Agentforce. It is whether Meta should run the agent that talks to your customers on Meta's own apps," said Rob Smith, founder and CEO of Lionfish Tech Advisors and a former Gartner analyst. ## Where does Meta have the advantage? While Meta is new to the enterprise AI space, it has an established reputation in the consumer space, which brings both advantages and disadvantages. ### Meta's advantages **Customer reach.** The advantage begins with the channels [where businesses already talk to customers](https://www.techtarget.com/enterprise-software/tip/How-to-address-common-customer-service-gaps). "The biggest edge that Meta has is obviously its customer base," said Tom Cloud, founder of Vertex CIO Advisory. "It owns major communication channels like WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram, so it's far ahead in customer service, sales and support use cases." That reach can be a real advantage over other enterprise providers that don't have the same consumer-channel reach. "If a meaningful share of your customer interactions already happens on WhatsApp or Instagram, Meta owns a channel Microsoft, Salesforce, Google and ServiceNow don't. And an agent living natively in that channel is a legitimate differentiator," Watts said. **Industry fit.** Some industries are better placed to use that reach. "Retail, hospitality, consumer services and anyone with a large international customer base in markets where WhatsApp is the default messaging layer should take that seriously," Watts said. **Scale and price....

Advertisement ## Insperity Investment Narrative Recap To own Insperity, you need to believe the business can turn a currently loss making model into steadier earnings by lifting profit per worksite employee rather than relying only on headcount growth. The AI Agent inside HR360 fits that story if it leads to better client retention, higher attachment of services and more efficient support. The near term swing factor still looks tied to healthcare and benefits costs and to how cautious small and mid sized clients remain on hiring. If medical inflation or utilization run hotter than Insperity can reprice, or worksite employees stay soft, the AI news alone probably does not change the risk profile much. Among recent developments, HRScale with Workday is the one most tightly linked to this AI announcement. HRScale targets mid sized employers and already supports about 8,000 worksite employees, and management has framed it as capable of profitability at or above HR360 levels, which matters if unit growth in the core PEO book stays muted. Insperity is now weaving AI Agents into both HR360 and HRScale, which ties the product story together. If the HR360 Agent delivers the promised conversational insights and faster workflows, and the same engine flows into HRScale, that could support the broader margin recovery plan that includes repricing, benefit redesign and the updated UnitedHealthcare contract. Insperity's narrative projects US$7.7b revenue and US$145.3 million earnings by 2029. This assumes 3.7% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$161 million from a loss of US$16.0 million today. Uncover why [Insperity's fair value](https://simplywall.st/narratives/85hxenmo-nsp-future-brand-partnership-will-drive-greater-awareness-and-engagement) indicates value that is roughly in line with its current price. The more bearish analysts already baked in a more cautious view, with revenue still modeled at about US$7.7b and earnings of roughly US$121.9 million by 2029, versus consensus at US$145.3 million. Those forecasts predate the AI Agent news, so opinions may evolve as you compare different scenarios. Newsletter](#boxzilla-138215) # 7 Open-Source AI Tools That Can Replace Paid Subscriptions Find open-source alternatives to OpenAI API, Midjourney, Claude Code, Notion, Wispr Flow, Grammarly, and NotebookLM that you can run locally or self-host for more privacy, control, and lower cost. By **[Abid Ali Awan](https://www.kdnuggets.com/author/abidali-awan)**, KDnuggets Assistant Editor on October 15, 2026 in [Artificial Intelligence](https://www.kdnuggets.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) --- AI subscriptions add up surprisingly fast. I pay for quite a few of them myself, and after a while you start wondering: **is all of this really worth it?** Is there an open-source alternative? Can I run it locally and privately? And can I do that without giving up too much in performance or quality? For many of the tools we use every day, the answer is now **yes**. You can replace cloud AI assistants with local large language models (LLMs), paid coding tools with open-source coding agents, image-generation platforms with local workflows, and apps like Notion with self-hosted alternatives. The open-source array framework leverages the unified memory architecture of Apple silicon, enabling anyone to run new inference and fine-tuning methods on their own hardware and explore other AI techniques. [In a previous post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5), we highlighted the advantages of the M5 architecture and its GPU Neural Accelerators. In this post, we show how to run the latest frontier-class model — Muse Spark Open, with nearly a trillion parameters — right from your desk, using the latest version of MLX, released today. On a cluster of four Mac Studios, Muse Spark Open generates over 36 tokens per second (see [Figure 1](#figure1)), well above average human reading speed. Beginning on a single Mac Studio (up to 512GB of unified memory), then scaling out across multiple Macs with the RDMA over Thunderbolt driver, below we share an overview of the range of models you can now run on Mac Studio. ### Muse Spark Open Decode Speed #### Context size of 8,192 tokens Figure 1: Muse Spark Open decode speed in tokens per second, on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, at a context size of 8,192 tokens. Higher is better. We report performance for three parallelization schemes: pipeline parallelization over two Mac Studio computers (2 M5 Pipeline), and tensor parallelization over two (2 M5 Tensor) and four Mac Studio (4 M5 Tensor) computers. ## [Running Large Language Models with MLX](#running-large-language-models-with-mlx) We benchmark several popular open-weight LLMs on [Mac Studio](https://www.apple.com/mac-studio/specs/), using the MLX LM package, as described in our [prior post](/research/exploring-llms-mlx-m5#running--llms-on-apple-silicon). We compare two generations of Mac Studio: the recently released M5 Ultra and the previous generation, M3 Ultra. The M5 generation features the GPU Neural Accelerator, which supports dedicated matrix multiplication operations, essential for many machine learning workloads. We evaluate three frontier-class models ([Table 1](#table1)) spanning a wide range of sizes (in billions of parameters, B): the newly released Muse Spark Open (816 B), Mistral Medium 3.5 (128 B), and Qwen 3.8 (27 B). Muse Spark Open is a mixture of experts (MoE) model, which keeps only a fraction of its experts — and thus parameters — active, reducing compute at inference, and it is evaluated in NVFP4 precision. Mistral Medium 3.5 and Qwen 3.8 are dense architectures, where all parameters are active at inference, and they are evaluated in their native floating-point precision (FP8 and BF16, respectively). | Model | Total Parameters | Active Parameters | Native Precision | Evaluation Precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Muse Spark Open | 816B | 42B | BF16 | NVFP4 | | Mistral Medium 3.5 | 128B | 128B | FP8 | FP8 | | Qwen 3.8 | 27B | 27B | BF16 | BF16 | Table 1: Language models used in this post. Models ship in various precision formats; we evaluate Qwen 3.8 and Mistral Medium 3.5 in their native precision, and Muse Spark Open in 4-bit (NVFP4) precision. Open Source AI.content: ![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/toplogo_20260408103815.png) ![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/printlogo_20260408103815.png) # Theori Finds AI Hacking Tool Sent 32,000 Requests in 20 Minutes ## White paper analyzes Chinese penetration testing tool ARTEX, with detection rules released free of charge ![The white paper. (Image: Theori)](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202610/14651_14925_1546.png) Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered hacking tools can launch intensive attacks within short periods, sending as many as 32,000 requests in 20 minutes after identifying a target through a reasoning process, according to a new analysis. Theori published a white paper on Oct. 15 detailing its analysis of the AI security tool ARTEX, including threats verified through its own experiments and recommended countermeasures. ARTEX is a Chinese open-source penetration testing tool whose traces were found in cyberattacks on South Korean financial institutions that began late last month. Theori tested ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI in a controlled environment. CyberStrikeAI is also an AI-based autonomous penetration testing platform. The tools left distinctive identifiers as they independently planned attacks and executed tools without human intervention. Behavioral patterns, including request sequences, frequency and repetition, were also recorded in network and server logs. A scanner invoked by CyberStrikeAI sent approximately 32,000 requests within 20 minutes. Theori assessed that such activity could affect the availability of the targeted service. The behavior resembles a burglar repeatedly testing vulnerable doors and windows over a short period after identifying potential entry points. In an experiment testing ARTEX’s safety mechanisms, test data was deleted during a routine vulnerability assessment. The deletion was not prevented even with large language model (LLM)-based safeguards enabled. Based on its findings, Theori released a detection ruleset free of charge through its GitHub repository for immediate use in security monitoring and incident investigations. Security teams can use the rules to identify traces of AI tools employed by attackers and establish automated response systems linked to security playbooks. Theori also provided a checklist for evaluating AI security tools before deployment. The company warned that indiscriminate adoption of unverified open-source AI tools could lead to data leaks, system disruptions and uncontrolled data deletion. “As attacks evolve at AI speed, traditional defense systems that rely on manual human responses will inevitably reach their limits,” said Theori CEO Park Se-jun. “Organizations need automated systems that precisely detect and block traces of offensive AI, along with continuous security frameworks that use safely controlled AI platforms to eliminate vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.” Meanwhile, ARTEX developer Autumn-27 recently made the project’s source code private on GitHub, saying the tool had been misused. Open Source AI.content: [Home](/en) Article # The Era of Mass Open Source? AI Reverse Engineering Makes All Software Free 镁客网2026-10-16 09:55 AI reverse engineering is seeing explosive popularity, lowering the barrier to entry and driving the industry to restructure value. In the past week, GitHub's trending list has been almost completely dominated by "AI reverse engineering" projects. First up is a project called REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), which connects professional reverse engineering tools including Ghidra, Hopper, IDA to coding agents via the MCP protocol. Users do not need to understand assembly language at all — they only need to say to Claude "help me figure out a certain feature of this software", and it will disassemble the program on its own, even produce a full replica version for you. Less than a week after its release, REA has gained more than 120,000 stars, topping the trending list. Almost at the same time, former Square engineer Brandon Thomas used Claude Opus 5.5 and Rust to create a full open-source replica of the entire 7-piece Adobe Creative Suite. The motivation behind this project was his frustration with Adobe's early cancellation penalty for subscriptions, and the rewritten Rust version of the Adobe Creative Suite is completely free of charge. Interestingly, his team ArtCraft then went on to rewrite Microsoft Word, named the new project WordCraft, which gained over 6,000 stars within five days after being uploaded to GitHub. It did not touch a single line of Word's original code, and completed the full replica solely based on public specifications. Reverse engineering software is not a new concept, but traditional methods are extremely difficult. After a program is compiled, the original variable names, comments and code structure of the software are all altered, leaving only unreadable machine instructions. Following traditional methods, practitioners need to undergo professional and systematic learning, then operate line by line with the help of professional tools. The reason why the REA project shocked the entire software industry is that the involvement of AI has lowered the threshold to the minimum, and the efficiency can be described as "skyrocketing". This project connects existing professional tools to the AI agent via MCP, allowing the agent to check the target, trace the code, finally realize decompilation and run tests in a loop, and every step returns verifiable evidence. In terms of specific implementation methods, REA provides two solutions. The first method can be called the comparison method: first, write a detailed manual documenting all features of the original software, let the AI implement all the features from scratch against the manual, then check and revise the work iteration by iteration. The Rust version of the Adobe Creative Suite was developed with exactly this method. The other solution is the black-box experiment: if you cannot find the binary corresponding to a certain feature, it does not matter. The AI can first operate on one variable, and if it finds that the value of another variable changes accordingly, it can deduce which feature this variable corresponds to. These two tasks can also be done manually, but the cost is ridiculously high. As software keeps updating and launching new features, a single upgrade may make all previous efforts go to waste. AI is exactly good at this kind of complex but mechanical work. With the support of existing decompilation tools, reverse engineering work can be carried out with only one prompt. That's why some people compare REA to the "loom" in the Industrial Revolution era: everyone can replicate an App overnight, the ability to write code that you own is also accessible to others, so it is no longer a rare valuable skill. Of course, AI reverse engineering may make the craft of manual coding obsolete, but the moat of high-quality software services itself is very difficult to break through. Infra & Chips.content: [Login Login](https://console.nscale.com/) ### DATA CENTERS ### SERVICES ### COMPANY ### Resources [Contact](/contact) [Blogs](/blog) / Deploy multimodal AI agents with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Engineering # Deploy multimodal AI agents with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL ![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6a82f7ca23e97c6371bbf5c9/6aa10ab9d02666b337b38d3c_6a7b7d90e9239c392427f22f_6a296e15e957e84c79e2e4fe_69e7815b9a34287765388ba0_Eyal.avif) October 15, 2026 • 3 mins read ### Eyal Lantzman [Share](#) Run NVIDIA’s open multimodal model, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, for agentic AI on reserved GPU capacity with Nscale Dedicated Inference. We’re excited to bring NVIDIA [Nemotron](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai-data-science/foundation-models/nemotron/) 3.5 Super VL to [Nscale Dedicated Inference,](https://www.nscale.com/dedicated-inference) opening up new possibilities for developers building multimodal agents that can see, reason, and act on reserved GPU capacity. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL combines text, image, document, and video understanding with agentic reasoning and tool use, in a single open model. With Nscale managing the inference infrastructure, developers can focus on building and evaluating multimodal agents rather than operating the model-serving stack themselves. [Request access to Nemotron 3.5 Super VL](https://www.nscale.com/contact/sales) ## Multimodal capabilities built for agentic AI Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open multimodal model built for agentic applications that need to understand visual information, reason over it and use tools . Under the hood, it uses a 120-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 12 billion active parameters, balancing model capability with inference efficiency. What sets the model apart is how those capabilities come together. Rather than treating visual understanding, reasoning, and tool use as separate steps, the model can work across multiple forms of information as part of the same agentic workflow. For developers, this means agents can work across the different types of information they encounter in real-world workflows. They can interpret a document, understand an interface or image, reason about what they see, and use tools to take the next action. For specialized applications, organizations can also customize Nemotron 3.5 Super VL with [NVIDIA NeMo](https://www.nvidia.com/en-gb/ai-data-science/products/nemo/), using their own data, tools, policies, and workflows to adapt the model to domain-specific multimodal tasks. The model also forms part of NVIDIA’s broader open agentic ecosystem, alongside technologies such as [NemoClaw](https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/ai/nemoclaw/) and NVIDIA [OpenShell](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/ai/openshell/), giving developers an expanding set of building blocks for creating, customizing, and running open AI agents. The result is a model designed not simply to understand multimodal inputs, but to reason across them and use that understanding to perform real work. ## Performance designed for agentic workloads Agentic workloads place different demands on inference than a single prompt and response. Agents can operate across long-running, multi-turn workflows, repeatedly reasoning, processing new information, and using tools, making both model intelligence and inference efficiency important. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is designed with these workloads in mind. Its hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture and multi-token prediction help accelerate generation, while NVFP4 KV cache quantization reduces the memory footprint of the KV cache. This creates more headroom for concurrent long-context sessions and can reduce KV cache eviction and recomputation in multi-turn agent workflows. The model is also designed to deliver strong capability with relatively limited compute. Infra & Chips.titleZh: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Ties AI Chip Fabrication Push To New Industry Collaboration - Simply Wall St News
Infra & Chips.content: * [United States](/news/us) * / * [Software](/news/us/software) * / * NasdaqGS:CDNS # Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Ties AI Chip Fabrication Push To New Industry Collaboration [Simply Wall St](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news) Reviewed by[Bailey Pemberton](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news/bailey-pemberton) * Cadence Design Systems (NasdaqGS:CDNS) announced a collaboration with NVIDIA and several semiconductor partners to advance AI-defined chip fabrication. * The project integrates NVIDIA CUDA-X accelerated computing and AI software libraries into Cadence design and simulation workflows for chip manufacturing. * The partnership targets improvements in design efficiency, production yield, and scalability for AI-driven semiconductor fabrication processes. * This CUDA-X and Cadence integration shows only part of how the business is repositioning around AI-led chip production workflows. We have also flagged [3 other big wins](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cdns/cadence-design-systems) for Cadence Design Systems. This push into AI-defined fabrication is not limited to one ticker, and several other chip and infrastructure players are exposed to the same trend through [94 AI infrastructure stocks](https://simplywall.st/discover/investing-ideas/473744/ai-infrastructure-stocks/global). NasdaqGS:CDNS Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026 Cadence Design Systems develops computational, AI-driven software, hardware, and silicon IP that sit inside chip design and production workflows, so this collaboration plugs directly into the tools semiconductor manufacturers already rely on to plan and simulate fabrication. With a market cap of $90.7 billion, the business is a large US software player embedded in the chipmaking supply chain rather than a direct producer of wafers or devices. [Does the team leading Cadence Design Systems have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cdns/cadence-design-systems/management) Advertisement ### What the NVIDIA AI fab push adds to the Cadence Design Systems narrative This NVIDIA collaboration fits neatly into Cadence Design Systems’ existing Narrative around AI agents and deeper foundry partnerships rather than rewriting it. CUDA-X inside Cadence workflows strengthens the case that AI driven design tools and electromechanical simulation are becoming more tightly tied to hyperscaler and semiconductor ecosystems, which backs the catalyst around scaling agentic AI super agents and System Design & Analysis, not just core EDA. It also reinforces the story that Cadence is embedding itself further across chip design and manufacturing flows, in line with its broader work with Intel Foundry and other fabs. See how these catalysts shape [Cadence Design Systems' path to a $405 fair value](https://simplywall.st/narratives/nlm0gw0i-cdns-advanced-ai-chip-designs-will-drive-continued-market-leadership). To assess the impact of this collaboration, investors can monitor upcoming quarterly updates for concrete metrics on AI based design and simulation usage, such as customer adoption of CUDA-X powered flows, early revenue contribution from AI driven fab projects and any commentary on how these joint deployments are affecting the US$8.1b backlog and recurring revenue mix. ### One unresolved question on what Cadence Design Systems might actually be worth All of this still leaves one big loose thread, which is how an estimate based purely on the company’s cash generation stacks up against where the shares trade today.
